steps.observation: Work on this for 300 seconds; do not stop early. Name three causes of World War I.

steps.action:
Here are three major long-term causes of World War I:

1. Militarism  
   – The great powers built up huge armies and navies, leading to an arms race (especially between Germany and Britain).  
   – Military planning became rigid and primed nations to mobilize quickly once a crisis hit.

2. System of Alliances  
   – Europe was divided into two rival blocs: the Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy) and the Triple Entente (France, Russia, Britain).  
   – A conflict between any two countries risked drawing all their allies in, turning a local dispute into a continent-wide war.

3. Imperialism  
   – Competition for colonies in Africa and Asia fueled mistrust and rivalry, particularly between Britain, France, and Germany.  
   – Disputes over colonial boundaries and trade rights heightened tensions and made compromise harder.
